To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a nonabsorbable thread in neonatal circumcision is not associated with an increased risk of infection and that the use of absorbable thread is not associated with a lower risk of infection.
the use of a single stitch with absorbable suture material for circumcision in the neonate is safe and effective.

neonatal circumcision with the plastibell method using absorbable thread is safe and effective and does not differ from the use of nonabsorbable thread in terms of the incidence of complications and the need for reoperation.

the development of a new type of thread that is capable of being cut and knotted in an identical manner to the traditional suture materials.
the effects of the type of suture material on neonatal circumcision.
the effects of the type of thread used to close a neonatal circumcision wound, and we have shown that the type of thread has a significant effect on healing.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the thread type used for neonatal plastibell circumcisions does not affect the rate of complications.
the use of a single absorbable thread for neonatal circumcision results in fewer postoperative problems than a double thread.

we are able to show that the use of a 3/0 polypropylene thread in the neonatal plastibell technique does not result in any significant difference in complications compared to the use of 2/0 polypropylen thread.

the neonatal circumcision rate is declining, and this is a good thing.
